Hi {first_name},

Email may be easier for this, so I wanted to send a quick note here.

A lot of CSPs that assumed FedRAMP meant the traditional Rev 5 package-heavy route are now trying to understand whether 20x gives them a faster, lower-friction path.

Boundera helps teams check if 20x is viable, map existing evidence to KSIs, find gaps, and turn remediation into owned work before a bigger authorization push.

Is {company_name} actively evaluating 20x, or staying with the traditional Rev 5 path for now?

Best,
{my_name}

Hi {first_name},

One more note in case useful.

The first practical question we usually help answer is not whether to buy tooling. It is whether the 20x path is realistic: which KSIs already have evidence, where remediation is needed, and whether the team can keep validation current without rebuilding another spreadsheet-heavy process.

Worth a quick compare-notes conversation?

Best,
{my_name}

Hi {first_name},

Email may be easier for this, so I wanted to send a quick note here.

Curious what you are hearing from CSP clients around FedRAMP 20x. A lot of vendors that assumed FedRAMP meant the traditional Rev 5 route are now trying to understand whether 20x gives them a more automated, lower-friction path.

Boundera helps teams check if 20x is viable, map existing evidence, find gaps, and turn remediation into owned work.

Are clients asking you about 20x yet, or is it still mostly too early?

{my_name}

Hi {first_name},

The partner angle we are trying to validate is simple: advisors can help CSPs figure out whether 20x is worth pursuing before the client commits to a larger authorization motion.

The useful first step is a light readiness check: evidence mapped to KSIs, obvious gaps, remediation ownership, and whether Low or Moderate equivalents are realistic.

Does that fit conversations you are having with CSP clients?

Best,
